title: Effect-native runtime patterns and lint enforcement tasks
principles: Decode unknown input once at ingress with the owning Effect Schema, pass Contract.Type, and encode Contract.Encoded only at egress.
Use strict but pragmatic Effect code: flat, linear, sequential, lazy, composable, and explicit about absence and failure.
Choose time, state, collection, Layer, and optionality primitives by owned semantics rather than API-count goals.
Extend Bundjil's existing Oxlint plugin, Effect language service, and boundary audit; do not add another lint runner or wrapper.
Every lint rule requires one AST invariant, exact ownership, positive and negative unit plus installed-plugin fixtures, a false-positive matrix, migration, and safe autofix decision.
Do not create pass-through services, generic collection transforms, DTO mirrors, manual readers, unsafe casts, or helper/common/utils sprawl.
Run one mandatory five-pass audit only after both implementation ledgers are otherwise complete.

Use state transition and collection semantic evidence rather than Ref adjacency, native collection, index, or helper-name lint.

Close typed error channels by removing arbitrary defect causes from exported tagged-error Schemas, enforcing the diagnostic boundary, and replacing a validated-but-impossible adoption-manifest defect with its owning typed failure.

Correct report-only infrastructure drift identity provenance by separating static authority-policy custody from dynamic branded GitHub run identity and carrying the decoded manifest digest through the report and receipt.

Make reusable exported Effect operation trace ownership explicit: named Effect.fn for semantic work, Effect.fnUntraced only for justified leaves or delegates, and one import-aware rule rejecting direct exported Effect.gen functions.
Treat provider rejection objects as hostile property containers: inspect only non-accessor own values through a non-throwing boundary before constructing closed diagnostics.

Use one bounded SSE framing owner for proof and streaming, require a framed response.completed before emitting clean completion, match the exact media type, and hide private transport dependencies with Layer.provide.
Bound complete SSE events as well as lines, fold proof events into constant-size state, name the receipt count as events, and remove the remaining request-mapper root/runtime exports.
Count every SSE field toward the complete-event byte ceiling, accept LF, CRLF and CR framing, and constrain observed Photon transport status to the closed 100-599 range or unknown.
Decode terminal Responses events through a closed Schema union and one Match-owned sequence state machine that rejects failure, incomplete, error, duplicate terminal and post-terminal events.
Keep raw provider Content-Type and status text inside the HTTP adapter; successful metadata emits the closed text/event-stream literal and public errors retain only bounded status and fixed messages.
Measure the complete SSE event ceiling from exact consumed wire bytes, including LF, CRLF or CR delimiters and the terminating blank line.
Use persistent Effect Chunk accumulators plus explicit 4096 line-fragment and event-field ceilings to prevent sub-byte-limit quadratic copying.
Retain a pending carriage-return state across empty transport chunks so split CRLF framing remains one delimiter.
Own HTTP status, byte/event counts, sequence numbers and output indexes with bounded integer Schemas rather than finite Number.
Inspect every supported Codex package subpath with one path-specific raw-transport export denylist oracle.
Pin the credential-bearing Codex Responses client to the one owned HTTPS endpoint literal; configuration cannot redirect bearer credentials to another origin or path.
Constrain access-token and account-ID values to bounded visible-ASCII headers and map defensive Headers construction failures to one fixed secret-negative tagged error before any request executes.
Own arbitrary protocol JSON with an opaque Effect Schema declaration whose depth-limited validator cannot recurse beyond 32 containers; use it for tool parameters and SSE JSON before event selection.
Decode every recognized Responses event into one shared closed tagged union before proof or live mapping consumes it, so malformed recognized payloads fail identically.
Advance one exact zero-based expected sequence number for every JSON event and reject duplicate, regressing or skipped values before proof success or clean mapped completion.
Remove the unused package-private postResponsesStream convenience accessor while retaining the named service operation used by runtime composition.
Read Photon SDK success fields through the same hostile own-data-property boundary as failures, then decode a newly constructed application-owned object.
Require Codex function parameters to be a non-null, non-array object before accepting the bounded JSON predicate; boolean, number and string roots are invalid.
Accept only dense arrays and enumerable own data properties in bounded Codex JSON so Schema encoding cannot omit or synthesize accepted values.
Brand Codex access-token and account-ID values separately before redaction so TypeScript cannot interchange two valid secret domains.
Own UTF-8 BOM state once per SSE stream and treat a colonless data field as empty data; later BOMs and empty events cannot disappear before a clean completion.

Capture the expected proxy token in the service Layer, remove it from operation input, decode and redact the presented authorization at HTTP ingress, bound both values, and compare over one fixed-width loop.
Reject a repeated Codex function-call output_index before replacing mapper state or emitting a second tool-call identity.
Canonical JSON decoding and encoding must produce detached, deeply frozen, bounded ordinary data so caller mutation and stateful objects cannot change a previously decoded value.
Load positive header timeout, stream idle timeout, cumulative body byte, and SSE event budgets through Effect Config; enforce time with Effect timeout operators and interruption-safe streams.
Decode the public proxy request with exact excess-property rejection and accept only omitted or literal-true stream mode because the route always returns SSE.
Inline Bundjil workspace packages in app Vitest SSR resolution so source-condition tests cannot silently execute stale ignored dist output.

Keep recursive canonical JSON implementation unions private, derive the public protocol values from opaque branded Effect Schemas, and remove the SSE accumulator assertion so accepted values cannot regain a structurally forgeable or unchecked public type surface.

Require the canonical JSON declaration type side to accept only recursively frozen canonical containers so Schema guards, constructors and nested type-side validation cannot brand caller-owned mutable values without running the detaching transformation.

Make negative nested-boundary fixtures satisfy every earlier contract with valid decoded values, exercise the named constructor, and assert the exact request.tools[0].parameters issue path so failure cannot occur before the intended field is reached.

Close implementation-task lifecycle before beginning the terminal audit: the product index, task statuses, completion evidence and active plan must agree on the exact 25 completed implementation tasks.

A 401 recovery oracle must capture old and refreshed authorization, consume the lazy returned stream, and assert mapped terminal completion plus [DONE]; request count alone cannot prove credential recovery or a valid response.

Deep freezing is not canonical-JSON ownership: a frozen Proxy can retain provider-controlled enumeration behavior. Require package-private identity provenance for every transformed container, reject unowned frozen containers at type-side guards and constructors, and prove decoding detaches a hostile Proxy into stable encodable data.

Proxy availability fallback may recover typed Layer acquisition errors only. Replace catchCause with Layer.catch so defects and interruption retain their Cause, and prove live/local defects plus local interruption remain terminal failures while existing typed configuration fallback remains available.

An upstream body pull is progress only when it emits at least one byte. Filter zero-length chunks before the Effect stream idle timeout so periodic empty chunks cannot keep the request alive without consuming byte, event or framing budgets; prove timeout and finalization with TestClock.

Prove rather than assume rejected-response lifetime: both proof and streaming acquisition must close their HttpClient.withScope request immediately for non-2xx and rejected media, leave Response.bodyUsed false, and keep rejected body bytes out of typed errors. The existing scoped implementation satisfies the contract; a four-case abort-signal matrix owns recurrence.

Bound accepted-but-unclaimed response ownership without moving upstream status/auth errors behind HTTP response headers: start one Effect-clock ownership watchdog after validated headers, close the response scope at the configured idle deadline unless body subscription claims it, and signal the watchdog from every scope-close path. Prove an unconsumed accepted stream aborts without reading bytes under TestClock.

Start the unclaimed-body ownership watchdog only after status, media type and metadata validation. Header acquisition remains governed solely by its independent header timeout even when the configured stream-idle duration is shorter; prove delayed valid headers survive the idle duration, then body subscription claims and closes normally.

Treat Deferred.succeed's boolean result as the exactly-once response-body ownership decision. Only the winning subscriber may expose the upstream stream; a subscriber arriving after expiry or after another subscriber must fail with the fixed typed stream error before touching the one-shot body.

Keep lifecycle claims truthful until terminal closeout: an active plan and pending audit cannot be described as completed or accepted history. Restore current/pending wording before the restarted audit, then move plans, ledgers and indexes to implemented history only with the final receipt.
